settings.analysisModeDesc: Per-dimension is deeper, Grouped is faster.
settings.analysisModeHintGroupedBody: runs one consolidated pass that covers every dimension in a single AI call. It's faster and cheaper, but findings tend to be less detailed since the model is juggling every area at once.
settings.analysisModeHintIntro: Two ways to look at your code:
settings.analysisModeHintPerDimBody: runs a separate analysis for each quality area (security, maintainability, and so on). It uses more API calls and takes longer, but each dimension gets its own focused look.
settings.analysisModelsDesc: Optional. Anything you leave blank uses the model you chose above.
settings.analysisModelsDescLegacy: Override the AI model used by subagents during code evaluation. Leave blank to use the defaults.
settings.analysisModelsHintClaude: Want a different model for different tasks? Pick one per tier (Fast, Balanced, Thorough). Type `haiku`, `sonnet`, or `opus`, and Claude Code picks the latest version. Anything you leave blank just uses the model you chose above.
settings.analysisModelsHintCodex: Want a different model for different tasks? Pick one per tier (Fast, Balanced, Thorough). Anything you leave blank uses the model above, and a blank model uses the Codex CLI default.
settings.analysisModelsHintGemini: Want a different model for different tasks? Pick one per tier (Fast, Balanced, Thorough). For example, `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` for Fast and `gemini-2.5-pro` for Thorough. Anything you leave blank just uses the model you chose above.
settings.analysisPowerDesc: Pick which tier above the evaluation should use.
settings.apiKeyDesc: Leave blank to use the key from `~/.omlx/settings.json` (default `1234`).
settings.assistantEnableDesc: Shows the assistant button (✦) in the toolbar and enables the Ctrl+` panel. On by default.
settings.assistantModelDesc: Pick the model the assistant should use.
settings.assistantProviderDesc: Choose which AI powers the in-app assistant.
settings.automaticChecksDesc: Check PyPI/GitHub for new versions once a day
settings.clientDesc: CLI tool or API provider for analysis
settings.cloudModelHintCustom: Type the model id your API expects.
settings.cloudModelHintOpenrouter: Type the model id you want. From cheapest to most expensive, you might try `meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b-instruct:free`, `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4`, or `anthropic/claude-opus-4-7`. The full catalog is on OpenRouter.
settings.concurrencyTestFailedLlamacpp: The concurrency test didn't finish. Make sure llama-server is running.
settings.concurrencyTestFailedOllama: The concurrency test didn't finish. Make sure Ollama is running and your model is loaded.
settings.concurrencyTestFailedOmlx: The concurrency test didn't finish. Make sure omlx is running and your model is loaded.
settings.gradeFormulaDesc: Tune how violations and compliance turn into grades. Changes rescore all runs.
settings.installGeneric: Install this provider on your machine and restart Quodeq, and this tab will be ready to use.
settings.installHintClaude: Install Claude Code from Anthropic's official documentation, then restart Quodeq. Once `claude` is on your PATH, this tab will be ready to use.
settings.installHintCodex: Install the OpenAI Codex CLI from the official OpenAI documentation, then restart Quodeq. Once `codex` is on your PATH, this tab will be ready to use.
settings.installHintGemini: Install the Gemini CLI from Google's official documentation, then restart Quodeq. Once `gemini` is on your PATH, this tab will be ready to use.
settings.liveFindingsDesc: While a scan is running, show only the findings it produces. Findings reused from unchanged files stay in the final report either way.
settings.llamacppLoadFailed: We couldn't reach llama-server. Make sure it is running on port 8080.
settings.llamacppModelHintP1: llama-server runs one model at a time, fixed at launch by the `-m` flag. Whatever you started it with is what shows up here.
settings.llamacppModelHintP2: To switch models, stop llama-server and relaunch it with a different GGUF file. For speculative decoding (MTP), pair the target model with a smaller drafter via `--model-draft`.
settings.llamacppNoModel: No model loaded yet. Start llama-server with a GGUF file.
settings.llamacppOffline: llama-server isn't running. Start it with `llama-server -m model.gguf --port 8080`.
settings.llamacppSubagentsDesc: Estimated from your VRAM. Run a quick test for a more accurate number.
settings.loadedModelDesc: The GGUF currently loaded by llama-server.
settings.localApiModelsLoadFailed: We couldn't load your {provider} models. Make sure {provider} is running.
settings.localServerHint: This server runs entirely on your own machine, so nothing leaves your computer. Quodeq is a local-first app that respects your privacy.
settings.modeDesc: Choose light, dark, or follow your system
settings.modelHintClaude: Type `haiku`, `sonnet`, or `opus`. Claude Code will pick the latest version for you. If you want a specific version, just paste its full id. You can find them in Anthropic's docs.
settings.modelHintCodex: Leave this blank to use the Codex CLI default, or type a model id that your Codex account supports.
settings.modelHintGemini: Type the model id you want, like ``gemini-2.5-flash`-lite`, gemini-2.5-flash, or `gemini-2.5-pro`. The full list is in Google's docs.
settings.modelOverrideDesc: Override the default model for all operations. Leave blank to use your client's default.
settings.modelSourceDesc: Default follows your Analysis provider and model. Choose Custom to pick a different one for the assistant.
settings.needModelBeforeEval: You'll need a model before you can run an evaluation.
settings.noProvidersDetectedDesc: Install a CLI tool or configure an API provider.
settings.ollamaModelHint: This list comes straight from your local Ollama server. To add a model, download it with Ollama itself (for example, `ollama pull gemma4:26b`). As soon as the download finishes, it shows up here.
settings.ollamaModelsLoadFailed: We couldn't load your Ollama models. Make sure Ollama is running.
settings.ollamaOffline: Ollama isn't running. Start it with `ollama serve`, or open the Ollama app.
settings.ollamaSubagentsDesc: We make a guess based on your VRAM. Run a quick test for a more accurate number.
settings.omlxModelHint: This list comes from your local omlx server. To add a model, use the omlx admin UI at `http://localhost:8000/admin` or pull a model with the omlx CLI. Models show up here as soon as they are downloaded.
settings.omlxModelsLoadFailed: We couldn't load your omlx models. Make sure omlx is running.
settings.omlxNoModels: omlx didn't return any models. Enter the model name directly (e.g. from your omlx admin UI).
settings.omlxOffline: omlx isn't running. Start it with `omlx serve`, or open the omlx menu bar app.
settings.omlxSubagentsDesc: We make a guess based on your unified memory. Run a quick test for a more accurate number.
settings.pickModelToStart: Pick a model to get started.
settings.pickModelYouWant: Pick the model you want to use.
settings.providerHintP1: Quodeq works with several AI providers, but you need to install each one before you can use it.
settings.providerHintP2: For the CLI tools (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini), install them on your machine and they show up here ready to go. Ollama needs to be running locally. Cloud providers like OpenRouter need an API key set up.
settings.providerHintP3: Greyed out tabs below mean that provider isn't installed yet.
settings.providerRunsDesc: Choose which AI runs your evaluations.
settings.providersLoadFailed: We couldn't load your AI providers. Make sure the server is running.
settings.restartDesc: Stop the server with `Ctrl+C` in the terminal, then run `quodeq dashboard` to restart. This page will reconnect automatically.
settings.serverAddressDesc: Leave blank to use the default (`http://localhost:8000`).
settings.subagentsDescRemote: How many subagents work side by side. Pick a number from 1 to 10.
settings.subagentsHintOllamaP1: Quodeq splits an evaluation into separate checks (one for each quality dimension) and runs them at the same time. More subagents means a faster run, but it also uses more memory at once.
settings.subagentsHintOllamaP2: Your VRAM sets the real ceiling here. Use Auto-detect to let Quodeq pick a safe default, or run a quick test to see what your hardware can comfortably handle.
settings.subagentsHintRemoteP1: Quodeq splits an evaluation into separate checks (one for each quality dimension) and runs them at the same time. More subagents means a faster run, but it also means more requests in flight.
settings.subagentsHintRemoteP2: Your AI provider sets its own concurrency limits, so the number you pick here is the most Quodeq will try to run at once. The provider may queue or throttle some of them.
settings.terminalEnableDesc: Shows a shell (❯_) in the toolbar drawer. Ctrl+Shift+` opens it. Localhost only; on by default.
settings.terminalRestartDesc: One persistent shell, started in your home directory. Restart kills it and opens a fresh, empty shell.
settings.thisModelEveryStep: This model handles every step of your evaluation.
settings.timeLimitDesc: Stop the evaluation after this long. You'll still see whatever finished in time, and the next run continues from there.
settings.timeLimitHintBase: Most of the token usage happens during the analysis phase, so this is your main way to keep a run short. Whatever finished in time still shows up in your results, and the next evaluation picks up from where this one stopped instead of starting over.
settings.timeLimitHintCloud: Heads up: a cloud evaluation runs against your own provider plan. The longer it runs, the more tokens you'll use. On a long codebase that can add up fast, so keep an eye on your usage and start with a tighter limit if you're not sure.
settings.typeModelIdDesc: Type the model id you want to use.
settings.verifyFindingsDesc: Recheck findings from earlier runs against your current code.
settings.verifyHintIntro: When you re-run an evaluation, Quodeq can check whether findings from earlier runs still apply.
settings.verifyHintOffBody: every run starts fresh. Previous findings are ignored, so you'll only see what the current run discovers. Faster, but you lose the history between runs.
settings.verifyHintOnBody: findings in files you haven't touched are kept as is. Findings in files that changed are sent to a quick AI check against your current code, so confirmed ones carry forward and stale ones get dropped automatically.
